html:
The Russian conquest of Siberia was the push of Russian rule from the Urals to the Pacific, from the 1580s to the late 1700s.

It began when Yermak and his Cossacks broke the Khanate of Sibir in 1582. After that, small parties of Cossacks and fur hunters moved fast along the great rivers, building wooden forts as they went: Tobolsk in 1587, Tomsk in 1604, Yakutsk in 1632. By 1639 Russians had reached the Pacific coast.

The motive was fur. The local peoples had to pay a tribute in sable skins called yasak, and furs became one of the state's biggest sources of money. Many peoples were hit hard by war and new diseases.

On the Amur River the Russians met the Qing and were pushed back. The Treaty of Nerchinsk of 1689 and the Treaty of Kyakhta of 1727 fixed the border. In the far northeast the Chukchi held out the longest. Farmers and exiles followed the fur men, slowly making Siberia Russian.
sum: The Russian conquest of Siberia was the push of Russian rule from the Urals to the Pacific, from the 1580s to the late 1700s.
